messages:
maria (support): FYI, large customer (acct: velox.ai) reporting p95/p99 spikes since we flipped quantization profile to int8 on the LlamaX-30b variant. They see tail latency jump ~2x for certain prompts. ticket: #4827
ken (runtime): Thanks — any traces/metrics from Redwood Console? can you paste the p50/p95/p99 before/after?
maria (support): Sure — from their dashboard and our telemetry after 2026-12-08 22:00 UTC when we rolled int8 by default to reduce costs:
```
// before (fp16 profile, baseline)
p50: 92ms
p95: 230ms
p99: 420ms
// after (int8 profile enabled)
p50: 95ms
p95: 490ms
p99: 1200ms
```
maria (support): Customer says availability is fine but tail latency causes timeouts in their user flows.
li (ml): Those numbers look like quantization-induced slower kernels or cache-miss regressions. Did we switch kernel implementation for some seq lengths?
ken (runtime): We did swap to int8-dequant-run path for that variant; there's a new fused-kv-kernel in the canary. deploy-bot: canary deploy 2026-12-08T21:55:23Z -> rolling int8 kernels to 30% capacity :information_source:  
olivia (sre): On SRE side, I see an increase in tail queueing on the hosting pool serving the model around the same time. p95 latency correlates with increased GPU kernel time for long prompts (>=1024 tokens).
raj (oncall): Can we repro locally with same model + int8 profile? If yes, we should revert the rollout and open hotpatch.
li (ml): Repro steps I used locally (worked on my workstation):
1) checkout model variant: llamaX-30b@v20261208-int8
2) run representative batch of prompts (mix short/long):
```
python tests/repro_latency.py --model llamaX-30b --profile int8 --batch-size 8 --seq-lens 64 256 1024 2048
```
Observed similar p99 regressions on my machine after warmup.
ken (runtime): Interesting — I instrumented kernel timings, here's a snippet of the kernel duration histogram (int8 vs fp16):
```
int8.kv_fuse_kernel: mean=7.2ms p95=30ms p99=260ms
fp16.kv_fuse_kernel: mean=4.1ms p95=9.8ms p99=18.5ms
```
ken (runtime): Looks like int8 path has pathological tail runs; possibly due to calibration loss causing extra slow path per sequence (lock contention or extra conversion).
li (ml): I suspect calibration procedure used a non-representative dataset and triggered fallback checks at runtime, causing per-request calibration validation and re-quantization for some layers. That would be bad.
maria (support): Customer logs show repeated "calibration-fallback" messages in agent logs: `quant:calibrate:layer_7: fallback_unstable`
ken (runtime): OK that's the smoking gun. The runtime is performing lazy re-calibration when offline calibr data invalid detected. We intended to do offline calibration during build/push. For safety we left a runtime path to validate but it's too heavy at scale.
olivia (sre): Mitigations? Can we disable runtime re-calibration and force model to use fp16 fallback for now?
ken (runtime): Proposed short-term mitigations:
- Pause int8 rollout for llamaX-30b (rollback canary).
- Disable runtime calibration check via flag: `--quant-runtime-validation=false` on hosting pool.
- For impacted customer, pin profile to `fp16` in their routing policy (can do immediately).
- Hotfix: change fallback to non-blocking (async) and add exponential backoff to per-layer validation.
li (ml): Also recommend rebuilding int8 artifact with a representative calibration set (500 samples from production prompts) and run the calibration validator in CI. Don't enable lazy runtime re-calibration.
raj (oncall): I'll open a rollback and a customer config change now. Maria, can you inform the customer about pinning to fp16 and ETA for rollback?
maria (support): On it. Messaging: "We've paused the int8 rollout for your tenant and pinned your model to fp16. We're rolling back the kernel change and will follow up once we complete a safe rebuild of the int8 profile with improved calibration." :white_check_mark:
deploy-bot: rollback started at 2026-12-08T23:12:01Z -> rolling back canary to 0% :truck: 
ken (runtime): Action items for us:
- Patch runtime to disable lazy calibration validation: runtime PR #7843 (in progress).
- Rebuild quant artifacts with curated calib set: li to own.
- Add telemetry alert that spikes if p95 > 2x baseline for 15m for quantized variants.
li (ml): I'll create a calib set from customer anonymized prompts, run batch calibrate with this command and push artifact after CI checks:
```
redwood-optimize calibrate --model llamaX-30b --samples 500 --out artifacts/llamaX-30b-int8-calib-v2
```
li (ml): We should also add a preflight validation step: run the rebuilt artifact through the internal latency harness comparing fp16 vs int8 across seq len distribution; require p99_int8 <= 1.3 * p99_fp16.
olivia (sre): For immediate mitigation, I patched hosting pool config to set `--quant-runtime-validation=false` and increased per-host request timeout to avoid cascading fails.
raj (oncall): After rollback started, customer reported improvement: new metrics after pin to fp16:
```
p50: 90ms
p95: 240ms
p99: 430ms
```
maria (support): Customer confirmed reduced timeouts in their integration tests. They want follow-up before we re-enable int8.
ken (runtime): Agreed — we won't re-enable wide int8 until rebuilt artifact and CI latency gate pass. We'll also add better logging for calibration fallback (rate-limit logs).
li (ml): Long-term: consider an async calibration service that maintains precomputed quant tables and serves them to runtime without per-request work. Also, add a versioned quant profile with metadata: calibration_dataset_id, date, sample_distribution.
maria (support): I'll coordinate with customer for acceptance testing and let them know the criteria (no >10% p95 increase vs fp16 on their workload across 48h).
ken (runtime): I'll follow up with PR+#7843 and a postmortem note in /postmortems once we finish. Thanks everyone.
olivia (sre): Adding incident tag and tracking to incident board. :memo: 
maria (support): closing loop with customer now. · :phone:  
raj (oncall): closing thread but keeping follow-ups assigned.
